topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the subject of cancer therapy and sets out the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles, clinical successes, and biological limitations of standard cancer treatments such as surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Targeting Tumor Vulnerabilities and Repair Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone dependencies, cell-cycle checkpoint alterations, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule inhibitors against oncogenic driver kinases and managing the molecular mechanisms of acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how engineered antibodies are used to directly target tumor surface antigens or deliver linked cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and strategies to recruit or engineer T cells to destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: Current Challenges, Trends, and Future Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the ongoing challenges of tumor heterogeneity, historical improvements in survival, and future strategic and ethical considerations in cancer treatment.
